source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 76 to 88. Each question cites its item. Authoring batch for the ITE pool; review before trusting.

questions.q: Months of frequency, urgency and nocturia with a weak stream and hesitancy, urinalysis negative. What is started?
questions.why: Tamsulosin, alfuzosin or terazosin, whichever symptom group dominates. The storage drugs come in when the alpha-blocker leaves storage symptoms behind, after a post-void residual is checked.

questions.q: Which findings justify adding a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor for male urinary symptoms?
a: A prostate volume of 30 mL or more
d: Nocturia more than twice a night
questions.why: It takes up to a year to reach full effect, which is why the alpha-blocker is still the one that starts first.

questions.q: A man on an alpha-blocker still has urgency and frequency. What is considered next?
questions.a: An anticholinergic or beta-3 agonist, after a residual
d: Stopping the alpha-blocker for a drug holiday
questions.why: Alone or combined with the alpha-blocker. Daily tadalafil has a place when erectile dysfunction coexists, but it is not the step for storage symptoms.

questions.q: A 5-day-old exclusively breastfed infant, feeding 10 to 12 times a day. Which finding means feeding is inadequate?
d: Nipple pain in the first 15 seconds of a feed
questions.why: After day four the targets are six or more wet nappies and three or more stools. Breasts that look soft or small prove nothing; no breast change at all by day five might.

questions.q: Beyond what loss from birth weight does a breastfed newborn's weight become a concern?
questions.why: Loss is expected for the first three days; loss that continues after day three is a concern at any percentage.

questions.q: How much nipple pain at the start of a breastfeed is normal?
questions.why: Pain that persists past the first minute needs the latch looked at. If formula supplementation becomes necessary, it follows the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine protocol.

questions.q: A healthy 25-year-old, four days of fever and cough, rapid test positive for influenza B. What is the treatment?
questions.why: Antivirals are not recommended for low-risk patients presenting more than 48 hours after onset. Rimantadine has no activity against influenza B in any case.

questions.q: What do neuraminidase inhibitors achieve for low-risk influenza patients treated as outpatients?
questions.a: No reduction in hospitalisation or death
d: About half the risk of pneumonia
questions.why: Systematic reviews including unpublished trials found no effect on those outcomes. Oseltamivir stays first-line for high-risk patients.

questions.q: Obsessive-compulsive disorder with an inadequate response to psychotherapy. Which drug is started?
questions.why: Fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, sertraline and paroxetine all carry the indication, and the doses needed are often higher than for depression. Bupropion, buspirone and quetiapine are not first-line.

questions.q: Where does clomipramine sit in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder?
questions.a: Approved, but too toxic for first-line
d: Not effective for the disorder at all
Used with an antipsychotic, not alone
questions.why: A tricyclic with the indication, held back by its toxicity profile rather than its efficacy.

questions.q: Which interventions have evidence for preventing falls in a community-dwelling older adult at higher risk?
a: Exercise, individual or in a group
Home hazard assessment with a validated tool
Multifactorial risk assessment with tailored interventions
d: Education about the harms of falls
questions.why: No type of exercise beats another. The multifactorial approach gives a small net benefit on average; the home assessment usually means a home visit.

questions.q: What share of adults aged 65 and over fall at least once a year?
questions.why: Falls are the leading cause of injury death in older adults, with over 300,000 hip fracture admissions a year, and a previous fall is the strongest predictor of the next.

questions.q: What is first-line treatment for symptomatic Helicobacter pylori infection?
questions.a: Bismuth, metronidazole, a PPI and tetracycline
questions.why: Optimised bismuth quadruple therapy. Vonoprazan with amoxicillin is the fallback for patients who cannot take it.

questions.q: What eradication rate does bismuth quadruple therapy achieve for Helicobacter pylori?
questions.why: Vonoprazan with amoxicillin manages 70% to 80%, which is why it is second choice.

questions.q: When may a clarithromycin or levofloxacin regimen be used for Helicobacter pylori?
questions.a: With documented susceptibility to the drug
d: In a patient with penicillin allergy
After one failed course of anything
questions.why: Resistance to macrolides and fluoroquinolones is common enough that empiric use of either is no longer recommended.

questions.q: A 5-year-old scalded on the arms and chest minutes ago, skin red and intact. What does the parent do first?
questions.a: Cool the burns under running tap water
d: Cover the burns with cool wet gauze
Apply aloe vera and leave uncovered
questions.why: For at least 20 minutes, after removing the clothing. Ice vasoconstricts and deepens the damage; wet dressings do not cool; aloe and NSAID gel are for pain afterwards.

questions.q: Up to how long after a burn does cooling under running water still help?
questions.why: Ideally within the first 30 minutes. Cooling reduces burn depth, shortens healing and lowers the need for grafting.

questions.q: Which features indicate a full-thickness burn?
a: Less pain than a shallower burn
questions.why: Superficial burns blanch and hurt; superficial partial-thickness burns blister and weep; deep partial-thickness burns are dry and do not blanch. The deep partial and full-thickness ones go to a burn centre.

questions.q: Why does a direct oral anticoagulant for a first DVT need no heparin lead-in?
d: It is given together with aspirin
It is loaded over the first week
It is easily reversed if bleeding occurs
questions.why: Less major bleeding and less monitoring than warfarin complete the case for it as outpatient monotherapy.

questions.q: A direct oral anticoagulant is unaffordable for a first DVT. What is the outpatient alternative?
questions.a: LMWH overlapping warfarin until the INR is therapeutic
d: Warfarin alone, with weekly INR checks
Unfractionated heparin in hospital for five days
Aspirin until the warfarin takes effect
questions.why: The low molecular weight heparin is started with the warfarin and stopped once the INR reaches goal. Admission for intravenous heparin is how it used to be done.

questions.q: Which are risk factors for breast cancer?
a: A first-degree relative with breast cancer
questions.why: Childhood chest radiation, especially whole-lung, carries the highest risk of the list. A grandmother with breast cancer is too distant to count on its own.

questions.q: Why do dense breasts on mammography raise the risk of breast cancer?
questions.why: Density is the proportion of glandular and stromal tissue to fat. It also hides tumours, which is a separate problem from causing them.

questions.q: Low mood, anhedonia and hypersomnia six weeks after an ischaemic stroke. With talk therapy, what is first-line?
questions.why: Post-stroke depression affects 20% to 60% of patients depending on how and when it is counted. Bupropion is for SSRI failure or intolerance; magnetic stimulation has growing evidence but is not first-line.

questions.q: Nortriptyline worked in trials of post-stroke depression. Why is it not preferred?
d: It raises the risk of a second stroke
It cannot be combined with talk therapy
It takes twice as long to act
questions.why: SNRIs and vortioxetine are the other alternatives when an SSRI is not suitable.

questions.q: Which patient on a modest opioid dose should still be offered naloxone and overdose education?
d: One on a three-day course after dental work
One on hospice morphine as needed
One on nightly alprazolam with no opioid
questions.why: The other triggers are a history of substance use or overdose, 50 MME a day or more, a benzodiazepine taken with the opioid, and a taper with loss of tolerance.

questions.q: Why is a patient tapering off opioids offered naloxone?
questions.a: Tolerance falls, so a relapse to the old dose can overdose
d: Tapering doubles the chance of a benzodiazepine prescription
Naloxone eases the symptoms of withdrawal
questions.why: The risk is the return to a higher dose, not the taper itself. Naloxone precipitates withdrawal rather than easing it.

questions.q: Sweating, shaking and faintness, glucose 52, an hour or two after sugary drinks, after gastric bypass. What is it?
questions.why: Rapid carbohydrate absorption drives an exaggerated insulin surge. An insulinoma causes hypoglycaemia regardless of meals; gastroparesis delays emptying and does not drop the glucose.

questions.q: Which features belong to early rather than late dumping syndrome?
a: Onset within 30 to 60 minutes of eating
d: A glucose of 50 mg/dL during the episode
questions.why: Early dumping is fluid shift and gut hormone release from rapid transit. Dumping of one kind or another affects about 40% of patients after bariatric surgery.

questions.q: A 10-month-old with a fever of 39.2 and a bulging left eardrum, hives to amoxicillin before. What is prescribed?
questions.why: A temperature of 39 or more is a severe criterion, so antibiotics are due even for one ear. Cefuroxime, cefpodoxime and ceftriaxone are the other alternatives; sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim no longer works against pneumococcus.

questions.q: When does acute otitis media get amoxicillin-clavulanate instead of amoxicillin?
a: Purulent conjunctivitis at the same time
questions.why: The three call for beta-lactamase cover. Ciprofloxacin is not used in children at all.

questions.q: Which child with acute otitis media may be observed without antibiotics?
d: A child with otalgia for three days
questions.why: Under 24 months, bilateral disease is treated even without severe symptoms. Severe means moderate or severe otalgia, otalgia beyond 48 hours, or a temperature of 39 or more.
